text:
Statements will cover topics including critical minerals, cancer research and online child protection.

PARIS — Heads of state at the next G7 Summit are set to endorse declarations on specific issues, spanning from health to critical minerals, while geopolitical talks will be addressed in a statement by the French presidency.

Leaders will meet in Evian, France, on June 15-17 and are expected to agree on ad hoc declarations on topics including critical minerals, research to fight cancer, online child protection, international solidarity, social impact investment and investment de-risking in fragile countries, the office of French President Emmanuel Macron said Thursday.

However, discussions on global imbalances, the crisis in the Middle East, the blockade of the Hormuz Strait and the war in Ukraine will be reflected in a statement by the French presidency, rather than a joint communiqué signed by all leaders. Last year, the Canadian presidency adopted the same solution for the G7 summit in Kananaskis.

"When it comes to substance, this G7 summit is already a success," an official from Macron's office added, stressing that France managed to start a dialogue with Chinese authorities and the G7 on tackling global economic imbalances.

On Thursday afternoon, Macron hosted an online meeting with representatives of G7 countries — including German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney — and officials from non-G7 countries including Chinese Vice Premier Zhang Guoqing.

France has been particularly vocal in calling on the EU to boost its trade defense arsenal to protect its industry against the flood of Chinese imports.

During the call on Thursday, participants agreed on the need to fix global imbalances and to continue discussing the topic at the G20 level with the support of the International Monetary Fund.

Frequent, expensive natural disasters are testing Europe’s ability to protect itself against the cost of global warming.

Romanian fighter jets shot down drones in separate incidents on Friday and Saturday.

For days, France and Spain have been fighting raging wildfires.

Guido Crosetto strongly praised Mykhailo Fedorov, who has been credited with bringing a technology overhaul to Ukraine’s military but also clashed with top generals.
